target_customer: Patients with end-stage renal disease and the nephrology and transplant system that would treat them; pharma-style licensing and partners
problem: Dialysis is burdensome and transplant organs are scarce; Trestle aims to implant bioengineered kidney tissue that supplements renal function and delays or avoids dialysis and transplant.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing a therapeutic tissue product; funded by grants, prizes and venture capital, with planned clinical development and partnering
product_category: Regenerative medicine and bioprinted kidney tissue

founders.name: Ben Shepherd
founders.background_notes: Vascular biologist and tissue engineer; YC page and company site.

founders.name: Alice Chen
founders.background_notes: Stem cell and 3D bioprinting scientist with 20+ years of research experience.

investors: KidneyX Innovation Accelerator (Artificial Kidney Prize Phase 2)

competitors.name: The Kidney Project (UCSF)
competitors.what: Academic effort to build an implantable bioartificial kidney combining a hemofilter and a bioreactor of kidney cells
competitors.traction_then: Academic prototype program; FDA accelerated review selection in 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: Bioengineering implantable human kidney tissue from stem cells with bioprinting is research-grade and years from clinical use; it requires regulatory approval pathways.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed university technology (Harvard bioprinting, Kumamoto stem cell methods, 2022) plus deep domain expertise and a long regulatory path make copying hard.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; in March 2025 it announced a research collaboration with Humacyte.

market_need_then: End-stage renal disease patients depend on dialysis and wait for scarce transplants; the KidneyX Artificial Kidney Prize created a funded demand signal for dialysis alternatives.

branding.name_origin: A third-party directory page reads the name as a bridge resting on interconnected braces, representing reliance on others' labs; this is an interpretation, not a company statement.
branding.domain_note: Uses trestlebio.com, with a bio suffix; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; the site stresses stem cells, bioprinting and biofabrication

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting engineering metaphor name, but biotech brands are mainly judged on science and sources show no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Trestle is a two-founder preclinical biotech from former Organovo scientists that licensed Harvard and Kumamoto technology in 2022, won a 1 million dollar KidneyX prize in June 2023 and announced a research collaboration with Humacyte in March 2025. It is still active, with limited verified venture funding, so the outcome is unresolved and depends on preclinical and clinical milestones.
notes: Equity funding is poorly documented. An aggregator (Startup Intros) lists a 2 million dollar seed in September 2024 led by Lerer Hippeau, and others list a 125K seed in January 2021 and investors such as Draper Associates and Acequia Capital; none confirmed by a second source, so none are recorded as rounds. The company site names Wellcome Leap as an investor and supporter but gives no amount. Totals range around 1 million to 1.13 million in aggregators. The Humacyte press release page returned 403 and was read via search snippets. Education degrees (PhD) come from the company site titles; schools were not found. The UCSF competitor source is dated 2012 and shows the program existed before the batch.
